aifrontier_example_mapping.simple_user_instruction: Bring external AI Frontier materials into VectorFL space and test whether they reinterpret the repo.
space_aware_setup_should_infer: build lite cards and source index
write fast channel for Codex review
aifrontier_example_mapping.why_this_matters: User should not need to separately request every step: fetch, compare, negative drift, validation, reentry, Codex handoff. Existing space should provide the default flow.

core_correction: The target is not /goal itself. /goal is only an example of loop-like execution pressure. The real target is whether the VectorFL/Hermes structure can absorb large task setup by consulting space before execution so later usage can focus on doing, not repeatedly asking the user for micro review/test/direction.

execution_setup_layers.function: preserve user original and detect whether request is simple action, setup/build-up, external material reinterpretation, or maturation handoff
read quick board/full-history sync/lite cards/lens cards before making worklist
infer likely work stages, validation lanes, missing space refs, expected artifacts, and hold boundaries
create worklist from original + space + model reasoning, not from blank planning
decide local-only vs Codex retrieval vs later Codex maturation; block default provider-backed calls
execute local steps while writing receipts/deltas; do not re-ask user for every micro-stage if space already gives stable structure
publish Codex-readable reentry/quick board so Codex can mature space after execution without blocking Hermes

future_simple_instruction_target: A short instruction should be enough for Hermes to set up a first-pass test lane: original preservation, relevant space orientation, task decomposition, local validation, HOLD artifacts, quick board, Codex reentry.
problem_statement: If Hermes only handles one-turn execution, user must repeatedly instruct listing, validation, judgment, test, and direction. For external-material work like AI Frontier, that becomes a bottleneck. The structure should let Hermes use existing space to infer first-pass setup, test plan, evidence lanes, and safe boundaries from a simple instruction.
